How to Buy a Condo in Phuket, Step by Step

From first budget to the Land Office transfer
HomeGuidesHow to Buy a Condo in Phuket, Step by Step

Buying property · Last reviewed: 2026-11-23

Buying in Phuket follows the same broad path for most foreign buyers. This guide lists the steps in order, what normally happens at each one and what to check. Details differ by developer and by property type, so treat it as a map and not as a contract.

1. Decide budget, use and ownership type

Decide what you want the property for (living, holiday use, rental, long-term hold) and what total budget you have, including the costs listed in our purchase-costs guide. Freehold condominium ownership is available to foreign buyers within a quota; villas on land are usually structured differently.

2. Choose an area and a shortlist

Pick two or three areas first, then compare projects. Our location pages show the projects, advertised starting prices, construction status and nearby places for each area, and the Sale and New Projects catalogues let you filter by price, bedrooms and status. Currently 90 projects are listed, 52 of them pre-sale or under construction.

3. View or video-tour, and ask questions

Visit, or ask for a video walk-through. Ask for the current price list, the unit plan, the payment schedule, the advertised completion date and the foreign-quota availability in writing. Marketing images of new projects are often renders.

4. Due diligence

  • Developer: track record, other completed projects, company registration.
  • Title and licences: what the land title is, and the building permit status, with the help of an independent lawyer.
  • Foreign quota: remaining foreign-owned share of the building (condos).
  • Contract terms: delay penalties, refund conditions, what is included (furniture, fees).

5. Reservation

A reservation agreement takes the unit off the market for a short period against a booking fee. Our standard reference for new developments is a THB 100,000 booking fee, but each developer sets its own amount and terms, so read whether and when the fee is refundable.

6. Sale and purchase agreement

The sale and purchase agreement fixes price, payment schedule, completion and handover dates and remedies. For off-plan units a typical structure is a deposit on signing (our standard reference is 20%) and the balance in instalments linked to construction, but your contract decides. Have your lawyer read it before you sign.

7. Payment from abroad

For a condominium registered in a foreign buyer’s name the purchase money is normally remitted into Thailand in foreign currency, and the bank issues a foreign exchange transaction document that the Land Department asks for at transfer. Keep every bank document.

8. Transfer at the Land Office

Ownership of a condo unit is registered at the Land Office, where the transfer fee and taxes are settled. Buyer and seller (or the developer) attend, or a representative acts under a power of attorney if your lawyer advises it. Who pays which fee is a matter of the contract.

9. After the purchase

Register utilities, understand the juristic person’s house rules and fees, arrange insurance and decide on property management if you plan to rent the unit out.

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to be in Phuket to buy?

Not always. Viewings can be done by video and some documents can be signed through a representative under a power of attorney, but whether this is suitable for your purchase is a question for your lawyer.

How long does a purchase take?

It depends on the type of property. A completed resale can transfer much faster than an off-plan unit, which transfers when the building is finished. We do not quote a general number because it varies by project.

Is the booking fee refundable?

Only if the reservation agreement says so. Read the refund conditions before you pay.
